designSystem.title: The shared visual foundation for the website and client portal.
designSystem.intro: This page renders every token, primitive and state defined in docs/design/design-system.md and docs/design/patterns.md. It is the reference during development. It is intentionally not linked from production navigation.

colors.title: A small palette, used with intent.
colors.intro: Brand green is for actions and meaningful highlights only — never decoration. Green backgrounds always carry dark text; green text only appears on dark surfaces.

type.title: JetBrains Mono, tuned like an editorial type system.
type.intro: Headlines set tight and large; labels set small, uppercase and tracked. Body copy never goes below 14px.

components.title: Restrained primitives, aligned to the reference.
components.intro: Buttons, badges, cards and links. One radius family, 1px borders, and no decoration beyond what the approved designs use.

states.title: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
states.intro: No color inventions. Skeleton uses the line tone, empty states a dashed border, errors stay on the paper surface with strong dark emphasis.
states.loading: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
states.whenProjectExists: When a project or request exists, it will appear here.
states.tryAgain: Try again, or contact support if the problem persists.

darkSurface.title: Dark sections carry the same system.
darkSurface.intro: Primary text turns light, secondary turns fog, and green is used for highlights. Border line darkens to keep the composition quiet.

brandSurface.title: One brand section per page, at most.
brandSurface.intro: Green backgrounds carry dark text. Use this sparingly — it is the loudest surface in the system.

servicesPage.body: We build and operate software across the full stack: AI agents and automation, backend platforms, web interfaces, cloud infrastructure, data systems, and legacy modernization. One specialized problem or an entire workstream — the engineers doing the work are the ones you talk to.
servicesPage.engagementBody: SDK enters in two ways: a fixed-price audit that diagnoses a specific problem and proposes a path forward, or a dedicated engineering workstream where a senior team owns the implementation end to end. Hybrid arrangements exist for systems that need both diagnosis and sustained delivery.
servicesPage.engagementModel1Body: A scoped diagnosis of a specific problem: architecture review, migration path, performance bottleneck, or security review. Output is a written plan with priorities, risks, and estimated effort.
servicesPage.engagementModel2Body: A senior team embedded in your stack for a defined period. Weekly delivery, visible progress, and direct communication with the engineers building the software.
servicesPage.engagementModel3Body: Audit first, then workstream. The team that diagnoses the problem stays to implement the solution. No hand-off to a different account team.
servicesPage.whatWeDontDoBody: No juniors on your codebase. No account manager between you and the engineers. No offshore hand-off after the proposal. No engagement that depends on selling you a larger scope than you need.

workPage.body: You know when something in your stack is costing you. Here are the situations SDK is built for.
workPage.engagementsBody: Most engagements begin with a short conversation or a written summary of the problem. From there, SDK proposes a scoped response: a fixed-price audit, a time-and-materials workstream, or a hybrid model depending on the uncertainty in the system and the clarity of the goal.
workPage.lookForHeading: A clear problem and a team willing to engage with it.
workPage.lookForBody: The best engagements start when the client knows something is wrong but does not yet know the full extent. We look for teams that want to understand the mechanism, not just receive a slide deck.
workPage.lookFor1Body: Performance, reliability, cost, speed of delivery, or compliance. The problem does not need to be novel — it needs to be real and measurable.
workPage.lookFor2Body: Read access to the codebase, infrastructure, and the people who understand the current state. Without this, any assessment is guesswork.
workPage.lookFor3Body: Someone who can approve the scope, the budget, and the timeline. Not a committee — one person with the authority to move the work forward.
workPage.fitHeading: When SDK is not the right answer
workPage.fitBody: We say no more often than you might expect. SDK is not a body shop for overflow tickets, and we do not take engagements where the problem is not yet defined or the team cannot commit to the process.

howWeWorkPage.body: Every engagement follows the same four-phase path. The output of each phase is a concrete artifact the team can review, challenge, or approve before the next one starts.
howWeWorkPage.expectHeading: What to expect in each phase
howWeWorkPage.expectIntro: A visible deliverable at every stage, so there are no surprises at handover.
howWeWorkPage.understandBody: Business goal, stack, constraints and success criteria. Output: a short brief and a proposed scope.
howWeWorkPage.designBody: Architecture, scope, risks and milestones. Output: a technical plan with visible checkpoints.
howWeWorkPage.buildBody: Implementation with visible progress. Output: running software, reviewed in short cycles.
howWeWorkPage.handoverBody: Deploy, document and transfer ownership. Output: working system, runbooks and a knowledge transfer session.
howWeWorkPage.deliverablesHeading: What you receive at the end
howWeWorkPage.deliverablesBody: Every engagement ends with a transfer of ownership, not a hand-off to a maintenance contract. The team that receives the work gets the software, the documentation, and the knowledge to operate it.
howWeWorkPage.deliverable1Body: Deployed, tested, and running in your environment. Not a prototype, not a pilot — production-ready code.
howWeWorkPage.deliverable2Body: Architecture decisions, runbooks, deployment steps, and operational notes written for the team that will maintain the system.
howWeWorkPage.deliverable3Body: A structured session with the engineers who will own the system going forward. Questions answered, trade-offs explained, next steps agreed.
howWeWorkPage.principlesBody: These are not values on a poster. They are the constraints we operate within on every engagement.
howWeWorkPage.principle1Body: You speak to the engineer doing the work. No account manager, no project coordinator, no translation layer.
howWeWorkPage.principle2Body: Every two weeks you see working software and a written update. No black boxes, no surprise invoices.
howWeWorkPage.principle3Body: We will tell you if something is outside what we can deliver well. A fixed-price audit is often the right first step when the problem is unclear.
howWeWorkPage.principle4Body: The code, the infrastructure, and the documentation belong to you. We do not build dependencies on our continued involvement.

aboutPage.title: Senior engineering, direct delivery.
aboutPage.intro: France-based B2B engineering company. We build, modernize and operate software across the stack — backend platforms, cloud infrastructure, AI automation, realtime systems and internal tooling.
aboutPage.body: Founded in 2019, SDK Enterprises works with a small number of clients at a time. The team is senior-only: no juniors, no account managers, no hand-offs to offshore delivery. Most engagements are scoped as fixed-price audits, dedicated engineering workstreams, or ongoing modernization sprints.
aboutPage.approachHeading: Why we keep the team small
aboutPage.approachBody: When an agency grows past the point where the partners know every engineer, the account layer appears. That layer is where context is lost, timelines slip, and cost multiplies. SDK is structured to avoid that.
aboutPage.approach1Body: You talk to the engineer responsible for the work. No translation, no delays, no miscommunication between sales and delivery.
aboutPage.approach2Body: The team that designs the system stays through implementation and handover. Knowledge stays in one place.
aboutPage.approach3Body: Every SDK engineer is senior-level. We do not use client engagements to train less experienced staff.
aboutPage.beliefsBody: These are not marketing statements. They are the constraints that shape every decision we make.
aboutPage.belief1Title: Software is a liability until it is understood
aboutPage.belief1Body: Every line of code carries maintenance cost. The goal is not to write more code — it is to reduce the cost of the code that already exists.
aboutPage.belief2Body: We do not sell a fixed engagement type. We diagnose the system first: architecture, data flow, deployment, team, and constraints. Then we propose the engagement that fits.
aboutPage.belief3Body: Visible progress, written updates, and direct access to the engineers. Secrecy around delivery is a symptom of a process that cannot be explained.

enquiry.title: Start a project
enquiry.subtitle: Tell us what you are trying to build, modernize, automate or fix. We will reply within 2 business days with an honest assessment of fit and what it would take.
enquiry.body: The form collects the minimum information needed to respond thoughtfully. Nothing is shared outside SDK Enterprises, and you can also reach us directly at hello@sdk.enterprises.
enquiry.body2: We review every enquiry ourselves. No account managers, no qualification scripts, no hand-offs.
enquiry.nextStepsBody: After you submit the form, we read it ourselves. If it is a fit, we will reply with a short written assessment and a proposed engagement model. If it is not a fit, we will tell you why and suggest an alternative.
enquiry.nextStep1Body: We read your submission and check it against our current capacity and expertise. Usually within 2 business days.
enquiry.nextStep2Body: A short written response: what we think the problem is, whether it is a fit, and what the first move would be.
enquiry.nextStep3Body: A 30-minute call or an async exchange to clarify scope, constraints, and timeline. No pitch deck unless you want one.
enquiry.nextStep4Body: A written proposal with scope, fixed price or rate, timeline, and milestones. You sign, we start.
